title: Factorise a monic quadratic with negative middle coefficient

source_reference.notes: Original Edexcel 4MA1 Higher-style item for the Year 10 quadratics MVP. Edexcel pivot metadata applied.

student_prompt: Show your working and give your answer in factorised form.

error_category_mapping.diagnostic_sentence: The numbers 5 and 2 are right, but both signs must be negative because their product is positive and their sum is -7.
Your check changed -7x into +7x. Expanding the brackets should return the original middle term.

hint_ladder.title: What do the signs tell you?
hint_ladder.prompt: This quadratic has a positive constant and a negative middle term. Think about what that means for the signs inside the two brackets.

hint_ladder.title: Pick a starting move
hint_ladder.prompt: Start from factor pairs of the constant term, then decide whether both signs should match or differ.

hint_ladder.title: A common slip
hint_ladder.prompt: Many students find the right magnitudes but forget that a negative middle term changes the bracket signs. Check the product and the sum together.

hint_ladder.title: The general pattern
hint_ladder.prompt: When x^2 + bx + c has c positive, the bracket signs match. The sign of b tells you whether both are positive or both are negative. Apply this pattern to your expression; do not copy an example.

expected_solution_steps.expression: -5 and -2 multiply to 10 and add to -7
common_errors: uses one positive and one negative number
expected_solution_steps.diagnostic_sentence: The stuck point is deciding the signs of the factor pair.

common_errors: gets the correct numbers but wrong signs
expected_solution_steps.diagnostic_sentence: The stuck point is checking that the brackets expand back to the original expression.

mark_scheme_notes: Award 1 mark for identifying -5 and -2; 1 mark for the correct factorised expression.
examiner_report_notes: Common errors expected: correct numbers with positive signs, weak negative-number control when checking expansion.
metacognition_prompt: Before you start, what do the signs of the middle and constant terms tell you?
